fields.description: Issue includes editorials and local commentary on the public campaign to force Al Capone to leave Miami, arguing about legality, publicity, and civic consequences; political commentary on Dade County Republicans organizing for the 1928 elections; and a feature praising polite public servants in local law enforcement. Additional items discuss tourism and entry/exit fees in Havana, Cuba; local business and municipal matters (merchant price-cutting, city support for sports teams, weights-and-measures work, boiler testing, and milk prices); coverage related to the upcoming Elks National Convention in Miami (grandstand seat sales and convention decoration); and society/column material and letters to the editor.
